title: Animal bite
summary: Wash promptly for 15 minutes and obtain same-day assessment for rabies, tetanus, and infection.
sources: World Health Organization — Animal bites fact sheet and rabies post-exposure guidance
actions: Control life-threatening bleeding first. Otherwise wash and flush the wound immediately with plenty of soap and running water for about 15 minutes.
Cover loosely with a clean dressing.
Seek same-day medical care for assessment of rabies post-exposure treatment, tetanus protection, wound closure, and antibiotics. Do not wait for symptoms of rabies.
Report the animal, location, time, and any known vaccination status. Let the appropriate authorities handle or observe the animal.
Watch for increasing pain, redness, swelling, drainage, or fever and seek care if these develop.
prohibitions: Do not ignore a small puncture wound.
Do not burn the wound or apply herbs, acids, or home remedies.
Do not chase, capture, or kill an unknown animal yourself.

emergencyCall.text: Call emergency services for life-threatening bleeding; every mammal bite needs prompt medical assessment.
